author: reek
body: Positive guard for the capability granularity ruling (CapabilityProbe section 7.3): peek-byte and poke-byte access the program's OWN heap, and heap access is not I/O - they stay pure by design, even in enforced application code. This is deliberate, not a laundering hole: the type system cannot distinguish a heap address from a device register at a runtime value, so memory-mapped device I/O gets its own read-mmio / poke-mmio intrinsics carrying Device.Mmio (the error case lives in errors/cap-launder-pure-mmio). A pure-signature function using the heap intrinsics must keep compiling.
